## Context / Problem

Every recurrence of the schema-blind extraction class was diagnosed from a lucky console
capture; when the reask loop in src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py (the prompted branch of
`_pai_structured`, the `for _ in range(structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES + 1)` loop that ends in
`raise last`) exhausts `OUTPUT_RETRIES` today, the raw reply is discarded and the failure is
not replayable. The store's posture is that durable records carry no response text (usage-log
precedent), so capture must be opt-in and local — never a default, never in ticket events.

## Approach

On the FINAL structured-parse failure of the prompted reask loop (immediately before the
terminal `raise last` in `_pai_structured`, after the bounded retries are exhausted), when the
new config key `llm.parse_failure_artifact_dir` resolves to a non-empty path, write one
timestamped file into that directory containing the raw reply text (the last attempt's
`str(result.output)`), the model id, the contract (response-model) name, and the attempt count;
then append the artifact path to the raised error's message. Key unset (the default) → behavior
is byte-for-byte today's `raise last`.

**Config plumbing — `llm.*` is a RESERVED section resolved in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, NOT
core `src/rebar/config.py`.** `llm.*` keys are fields on `LLMConfig` (src/rebar/llm/config.py),
resolved in `LLMConfig.from_env` off the file table from `_read_llm_file_table` (which calls
`_root_config.read_reserved_section("llm", …)`), with the standard CLI > env > file > default
precedence provided by the `_llm_str` helper. So the key is added as a new
`parse_failure_artifact_dir: str | None = None` field on `LLMConfig`, resolved in `from_env`
via `_llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR", "parse_failure_artifact_dir",
None)` — exactly the pattern the file's other string knobs use (e.g. `base_url`). The failure
hook in `structured_run.py` obtains the resolved value on the failure path via
`rebar.llm.config.resolve_gate_config(...)` (the active gate config if a gate is running, else a
fresh `LLMConfig.from_env`), which is how the other helpers in that module already read config.

**Why this approach (rationale).** It reuses the one config-resolution path every other `llm.*`
knob uses (no new loader, no core-config coupling — importing `rebar.llm.config` is already on
the failure path), and it fails CLOSED and LOCAL: the default-None key means zero behavior
change and nothing is ever written unless an operator opts in on their own host, honoring the
usage-log "no durable response text" posture. The write is confined to the prompted branch
because the NativeOutput branch never runs the reask loop (constrained decoding validates
in-SDK), so that is the only reask-exhaustion seam. The write is BEST-EFFORT: it is wrapped so
any I/O error (missing/unwritable dir it cannot create, full disk) is swallowed and the ORIGINAL
`last` validation error is still raised unchanged — a debugging aid must never convert a parse
failure into a different, misleading failure. The directory is created if absent
(`mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`). Rotation is by count: after writing, prune oldest-by-mtime
so at most 20 artifacts remain per directory, so an unattended host cannot grow unbounded;
concurrent writers racing the prune is acceptable (best-effort, local debugging only). A
successful parse takes the `return` path and never reaches the hook, so it writes nothing.

Alternatives considered: (a) threading the dir down as a new `_pai_structured` parameter — heavier
signature churn across callers for a value only the failure path needs; (b) capturing in the
generic `interpret_failure` enricher — wrong seam, it handles typed provider errors, not the
prompted-parse-exhaustion path. The chosen in-branch resolve is the smallest correct change.

Document the key (name, default None = off, `REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR` env alias,
rotation-keeps-newest-20) in docs/config.md alongside the other `llm.*` keys.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py — the failure hook in `_pai_structured`'s prompted branch,
  before `raise last`; reads the dir via `resolve_gate_config`, writes the artifact best-effort,
  appends the path to the error message.
- src/rebar/llm/config.py — the new `parse_failure_artifact_dir: str | None` field on
  `LLMConfig` and its `_llm_str` resolution in `from_env` (the RESERVED-`llm`-section path;
  core src/rebar/config.py is deliberately NOT touched — it does not own `llm.*`).
- docs/config.md — key documentation (default + env alias + rotation).
- tests/unit/test_structured_run.py — new contrast tests (fault injected at the parse seam).

## Testing

Unit tier with config-effect contrast (shared test-design standard §6), fault injected at the
parse seam (a reply fixture that fails all candidates, forcing retry exhaustion), the model
driven by the `fake` runner / a stubbed agent so no live call is made:

- Key set + forced final failure → exactly one artifact exists containing the reply bytes and
  metadata (model id, contract name, attempt count); the raised error names the path.
- Key unset + same failure → no artifact, error byte-for-byte unchanged (negative control).
- Key set + successful parse → nothing written (success negative control).
- Rotation: writing a 21st artifact evicts the oldest (by mtime).
- Best-effort: an unwritable configured dir still raises the ORIGINAL parse error (the artifact
  write never masks it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Forced final parse failure with the key set writes exactly one artifact with reply +
      model id + contract name — checked by the new unit test.
- [ ] With the key unset the failure path is byte-for-byte unchanged and writes nothing —
      checked by the contrast test.
- [ ] A successful parse writes nothing even with the key set — checked by the negative
      control test.
- [ ] The key is documented with its default and rotation behavior — checked by the
      docs/config.md section existing and naming both.
